req.title: Return 404 on unknown post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-022 requires HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or POST /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id. Tests must: (1) positive — confirm existing post id returns 200 on GET update (logged in as author); (2) negative — confirm non-existent post id returns 404 on GET update, POST update, and POST delete; (3) boundary — use post id 0 (below minimum valid id) and a very large id (999999) to confirm 404 at numeric boundaries. All tests use pre-loaded data: post 2 belongs to user Rahul (id=1, password='stone'); post 999 does not exist. Login is performed via POST /auth/login before protected routes are accessed.

tests.name: test_get_update_existing_post_returns_200
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with 20 posts; post id=2 authored by user Rahul (id=1)
User Rahul is logged in (session cookie present)
expected: GET /2/update returns HTTP 200 (post exists, user is author)
trace: R-FLASKR-022: existing post id must NOT return 404
blog.update -> get_post(2) -> post found -> render update form
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login as Rahul who owns post 2
r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {r_login.status_code}'

# GET existing post update page
r = client.get('/2/update')
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for existing post, got {r.status_code}'

tests.name: test_update_post_id_zero_returns_404
preconditions: Database pre-loaded; post ids start at 1, so id=0 does not exist
actions: GET /0/update (id=0, below minimum valid post id)
expected: GET /0/update returns HTTP 404 (boundary: id below minimum)
trace: R-FLASKR-022: id=0 is below the minimum valid post id (1); must return 404
BVA: boundary at id=0 (min-1), id=1 (min valid), id=21 (max+1)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

# id=0: boundary below minimum valid post id
r_zero = client.get('/0/update')
assert r_zero.status_code == 404, f'Expected 404 for id=0, got {r_zero.status_code}'

# id=1: minimum valid post id (owned by James/user 5, not Rahul — expect 403 not 404)
r_one = client.get('/1/update')
assert r_one.status_code != 404, f'id=1 exists, should not be 404, got {r_one.status_code}'

# id=21: one above max pre-loaded post id (20)
r_above = client.get('/21/update')
assert r_above.status_code == 404, f'Expected 404 for id=21, got {r_above.status_code}'

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

large_id = 999999999

r1 = client.get(f'/{large_id}/update')
assert r1.status_code == 404, f'GET update large id: expected 404, got {r1.status_code}'

r2 = client.post(f'/{large_id}/update', data={'title': 'T', 'body': 'B'})
assert r2.status_code == 404, f'POST update large id: expected 404, got {r2.status_code}'

r3 = client.post(f'/{large_id}/delete')
assert r3.status_code == 404, f'POST delete large id: expected 404, got {r3.status_code}'
